question: What is the primary physiological goal of respiratory prevention strategies?

options.A: Enhancing the production of surfactant in adult alveoli
options.B: Decreasing the total surface area available for gas exchange
options.C: Preserving optimal lung capacity and minimizing tissue injury
options.D: Increasing the resting metabolic rate of pulmonary tissues

explanation: Respiratory prevention focuses on protecting lung tissues from damage and maintaining efficient gas exchange. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is primary respiratory prevention particularly critical in settings with high levels of indoor biomass fuel use?

options.A: It directly increases atmospheric oxygen levels inside residential homes
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent tuberculosis screening
options.C: It cures preexisting structural lung collapse within the first week
options.D: It prevents chronic exposure to noxious smoke that damages pulmonary airways

explanation: Biomass smoke contains particulate matter and irritants that cause chronic airway inflammation and damage over time. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h1)

question: What defines primary prevention in the context of respiratory health?

options.A: Stopping a disease process before it ever develops
options.B: Rehabilitating patients with established chronic bronchitis
options.C: Detecting early asymptomatic lesions through screening
options.D: Administering emergency bronchodilators during an acute attack

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and stopping the onset of disease entirely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: A patient asks why avoiding secondhand smoke is important even though they do not smoke themselves. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Inhaling environmental tobacco smoke still delivers harmful irritants that inflame your bronchial airways
options.B: Passive smoke exposure exclusively affects cardiovascular function rather than pulmonary tissue
options.C: Secondhand smoke causes immediate, permanent paralysis of the alveolar macrophages only
options.D: Inhaled tobacco byproducts are completely neutralized by nasal hair before reaching the trachea

explanation: Environmental tobacco smoke contains numerous carcinogens and irritants that trigger inflammation in non-smokers. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which pathogen is primarily targeted by the annual influenza vaccination?
explanation: The annual influenza vaccine specifically targets circulating strains of the influenza virus. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why must the influenza vaccine be administered annually unlike many other lifetime immunizations?

options.A: Annual dosing is required to activate the innate immune system exclusively
options.B: Storage temperatures in clinics degrade the vaccine formula every year
options.C: Antibodies produced by the vaccine disappear entirely within 30 days
options.D: The virus undergoes frequent antigenic drift and shift

explanation: Rapid genetic mutations in the influenza virus change its surface proteins, requiring updated yearly formulations. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of engineering controls in high-risk industrial environments?

options.A: Replacing standard medical therapy for acute asthma attacks
options.B: Increasing the rate of carbon dioxide elimination in workspaces
options.C: Removing or reducing airborne hazards at the source
options.D: Eliminating the need for employee health surveillance

explanation: Engineering controls aim to isolate or remove hazards from the work environment before they reach the worker. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which respiratory condition is classically associated with prolonged occupational exposure to silica dust in mining or construction?
explanation: Inhaling crystalline silica dust causes nodular pulmonary fibrosis, known clinically as silicosis. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary objective of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Rehabilitating patients with end-stage chronic respiratory failure
options.B: Administering routine childhood vaccines in community clinics
options.C: Early detection and prompt treatment of asymptomatic disease
options.D: Completely preventing the initial exposure to environmental pathogens

explanation: Secondary prevention catches diseases early when interventions are most effective at halting progression. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: Which diagnostic test is most commonly used to detect early airflow obstruction in individuals at risk for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?
explanation: Spirometry provides objective measurements of airflow rates and lung volumes, identifying obstruction before symptoms become severe. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention in chronic respiratory illnesses?

options.A: Preventing the initial genetic mutation that causes the condition
options.B: Reducing complications and maximizing the remaining functional capacity
options.C: Providing routine immunizations to infants in rural health posts
options.D: Screening healthy populations for early signs of asymptomatic infection

explanation: Tertiary prevention manages existing chronic disease to limit disability and enhance quality of life. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why is teaching pursed-lip breathing an important intervention during pulmonary rehabilitation for a patient with chronic airflow limitation?

options.A: It increases the total red blood cell count to compensate for low iron
options.B: It creates back-pressure that keeps small airways open during expiration and prevents collapse
options.C: It completely reverses scar tissue formation within the alveolar walls
options.D: It eliminates the need for any maintenance bronchodilator medications

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing prolongs exhalation and maintains positive airway pressure, helping trap less air in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which activity best exemplifies public health advocacy by a nurse in respiratory care?

options.A: Calculating the exact fluid maintenance rate for a dehydrated child
options.B: Participating in community outreach campaigns to promote clean air policies
options.C: Administering a prescribed intravenous antibiotic in an acute ward
options.D: Reading a patient's chest X-ray report independently in the records room

explanation: Public health advocacy extends beyond individual patient care to broader community education and policy support. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h7)

question: Why is a return demonstration considered essential when educating a patient on using a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: It fulfills a legal documentation requirement without impacting clinical outcomes
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never experience any drug side effects
options.C: It replaces the need for written discharge instructions entirely
options.D: It allows the nurse to verify that the patient actually performs the correct technique for optimal drug delivery

explanation: Observing a patient perform the technique ensures they coordinate actuation and inhalation properly for drug efficacy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h7)
